# School_Management_System — project context

## Purpose

Build a realistic school administration and fee management application while learning the .NET ecosystem. The system is for school administrators, admission officers, teachers, accountants, principals, and parents or students.

## Current state

Phases 1–6 are implemented in source. The Phase 6 migration is generated but has not been applied because the local MySQL service is unavailable in this environment. Phase 2 adds an anonymous admission form, private PDF/PNG/JPEG uploads, role-protected review, approval/rejection history, capacity-checked student enrollment, guardian records, status history, a paginated student directory, profile updates, and CSV export. Phase 3 adds subject and teacher assignments, teacher-scoped attendance, reviewed corrections, reports, and guardian-linked attendance. Phase 4 adds examinations, teacher-scoped marks, review and publication, grade bands, linked-parent report cards, and reasoned revision history. Phase 5 adds fee structures, active-enrollment assignments, approved discounts, invoice snapshots, partial cash/bank collections, receipt records, parent-scoped invoices, server-validated SSLCOMMERZ sandbox checkout, refund approval and status reconciliation, overdue reminder drafts, and school-timezone financial reports. Phase 6 adds atomic student roster and teacher marks imports with row validation, student and finance Excel exports, PDF invoices/receipts/report cards, role-protected student document ZIPs, audience-targeted announcements, parent-teacher conversations with private attachments, append-only application audit records, SMTP identity/reminder emails, and a hosted retrying outbox worker. The solution builds; Phase 2–6 browser workflows still need manual walkthroughs. SSLCOMMERZ flows need merchant sandbox credentials and a public HTTPS callback host. SMTP delivery needs credentials in local User Secrets or environment variables.

## Architecture

- C# on .NET 9 with ASP.NET Core and a Blazor Web App using Interactive Server rendering initially
- MySQL 8.4 with Entity Framework Core 9 and the Pomelo 9 provider
- ASP.NET Core Identity, role-based access, and policy-based authorization
- Four-project modular monolith: Core, Application, Infrastructure, and Blazor Web
- Initial data seeding for six roles and an optional Super Admin configured through User Secrets
- A modular monolith with logical modules for school setup, admissions, academics, finance, and communication
- xUnit, integration tests, and browser-based end-to-end testing as the project develops

## Main roles

Super Admin; Admission Officer; Teacher; Accountant; Parent/Student; Principal. Permissions must be checked on the server, including access to records belonging to a particular student or class.

## Planned modules

1. Implemented: school profile, academic years, classes, and sections. Phase 4 adds terms and configurable grade bands; the school calendar remains planned.
2. Implemented in source: admission applications, private documents, review and approval, students, guardians, and yearly enrollment history. The full manual admission workflow walkthrough is pending.
3. Implemented: subjects and teacher assignments; teacher-scoped attendance sessions and records; correction requests reviewed by Principal/Super Admin; daily and monthly reports; and parent attendance access through staff-managed guardian account links. Notifications remain planned.
4. Implemented in source: terms and examinations; teacher-scoped mark entry and complete-roster submission; review, approval, publication, configurable grade bands, linked-parent report cards, and reasoned revision history. PDF report card export is implemented in Phase 6. The browser workflow walkthrough is pending.
5. Implemented in source: fee structures, active-enrollment assignments, discount approvals, invoices, partial allocations, receipt printing, SSLCOMMERZ sandbox payment/refund flows, overdue reminder drafts, and school-timezone reports. SMTP delivery and scheduled overdue reminder queueing are implemented in Phase 6.
6. Implemented in source: validated student and marks workbook import, student and finance Excel export, protected invoice/receipt/report-card PDFs and student document ZIPs, announcements, parent-teacher messaging with private attachments, SMTP identity/reminder email, append-only audit records, and hosted background processing.
7. Security review, backup strategy, production configuration, and deployment.

## Core rules

- Use `decimal` for money and a consistent school timezone for date-based billing.
- Separate invoices from payments; only verified successful payments count toward balances.
- Keep admission, enrollment, payment, and approval operations idempotent and transactional where appropriate.
- Use unique database constraints to prevent duplicate attendance and marks records.
- Preserve result approval and revision history; published results cannot be silently changed.
- Store private uploads outside the public web root and authorize every download.
- Do not commit credentials, private student information, uploaded documents, or local databases.
